text:
Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for agreeing to evaluate this 15-year-old male whose clinical difficulties began in early infancy, with his initial presentation at approximately ten weeks of life. He is currently an active tenth grader who lives with his family, and his family history is entirely negative for chronic illnesses.

He recently developed a severe respiratory illness, and diagnostic bronchoscopy and chest CT confirmed invasive fungal pulmonary disease caused by Aspergillus. Initial lab work highlighted a profound depression across all three blood cell lineages, characterized by a severely depressed absolute neutrophil count and a substantially low platelet count. Extended immune profiling showed that his circulating levels of both IgG and IgM were noticeably reduced, and lymphocyte quantification demonstrated a striking reduction in total CD19-positive B lymphocytes.

A diagnostic bone marrow evaluation was obtained. The trephine biopsy revealed severely reduced marrow cellularity alongside active engulfment of hematopoietic cells by histiocytes within the marrow space. Immunophenotyping and morphology revealed no evidence of acute B-lymphoblastic leukemia, and acute lymphoblastic leukemia of T-cell origin was likewise completely ruled out. Physical examination and abdominal imaging confirmed that his spleen was of normal size, with no splenic enlargement detected. His baseline renal indices and liver enzymes remain within normal limits, and he is tolerating antifungal therapy without issue.

I would be most grateful for your clinical assessment and guidance regarding further management for this young man.

Sincerely,
Dr. Julian Hayes
